subject: SLO confirmation + streaming clarification — Acme demo follow-up
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Liu <samuel.liu@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLO confirmation + streaming clarification — Acme demo follow-up

Hi Samuel —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. I wanted to summarize the performance SLOs we discussed and confirm a couple of streaming details before we move to the synthetic validation stage. Below is what we captured from the call and the open questions we flagged.

Quick recap (what you confirmed during the demo):
- Target P95 latency for single-turn text generation: <= 350 ms (measured at the API layer, end-to-end).
- Sustained throughput target: ~120 requests/sec for peak traffic windows (burst to 250rps acceptable for short periods).
- Concurrency target: ability to maintain P95 at 50 concurrent sessions (KV cache expected to help).
- Streaming: chunked token streaming required for user-facing typing UX; soft goal is initial token delivered < 150 ms and per-chunk inter-token latency < 40 ms under target load.

Open questions for your engineering team:
1) Can you share representative payload sizes (avg tokens per request, max tokens) for both prompts and expected assistant responses? We used conservative defaults in the demo; real payloads will help our kernel selection and batching profile.
2) Are you using long-lived sessions with KV cache per user (yes/no)? If yes, typical session length in tokens or minutes?
3) Do you expect any synchronous reranking calls per request (additional downstream calls we should include in SLO calculations)?

Next steps I propose:
- I attach a preliminary SLO checklist (acme-slo-checklist.xlsx) and the demo recording. Please fill in the sample payload column and confirm session behavior by EOD Tuesday.
- We'll schedule a 60-minute engineering validation call to run a small synthetic test with your payloads — proposed slot: Thu 2026-07-16 10:00 PT.
- After validation we'll produce a short report with measured P50/P95/P99 and recommended batching/quantization profile for your Dedicated pool.

If that timeline works I’ll lock the slot and loop in our infra lead.

Best,

Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Liu <samuel.liu@acme.ai>

Date: 2026-07-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO confirmation + streaming clarification — Acme demo follow-up

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Typical prompt size: 40–120 tokens; average assistant response: 100–300 tokens. Peak workflows (multi-turn summaries) can go up to ~1,200 tokens but are lower frequency.
- We do long-lived sessions for chat; KV cache per user/session is important. Average session length is ~20 minutes (roughly 800–1,200 tokens across the session).
- We have a light-weight reranker that is invoked ~10% of requests (one extra call that adds ~50–80ms on our side).

Thu 7/16 10:00 PT works for us to run the validation. I’ll also CC procurement (contracts@acme.ai) after we confirm SLOs so they can start the procurement path.

One clarification on streaming: for UX we really need initial token < 200ms on first byte for warm sessions; per-chunk latency under load is a softer requirement (sub-80ms ok). If you think those numbers materially change the infrastructure plan please flag.

Sam
VP Product, Acme AI

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T13:21:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLO confirmation + streaming clarification — Acme demo follow-up

Monica / Priyom — forwarding Sam’s answers. Key implications:
- Average response tokens are higher than we tested in the demo (~100–300), and occasional 1,200 token responses exist. We should validate memory/KV impact on long sessions.
- KV cache per user + 20-minute sessions means warm cache behavior matters; include warm and cold runs in the validation.
- Reranking at ~10% adds a predictable latency tail — factor this into P95 budget.
- Streaming goal: initial token <200ms is slightly looser than our conservative 150ms demo target; still within achievable range but needs attention to batching and kernel selection.

Proposed validation checklist for the synthetic run (things Priyom / infra team should run through):
- Load profile: steady 120rps for 10 minutes, 30s burst at 250rps; measure P50/P95/P99.
- Concurrency sweep: 10 / 25 / 50 concurrent sessions with long-lived KV state; measure per-session tail latency and memory/KV usage.
- Streaming metrics: measure first-byte latency for warm sessions and per-chunk latencies under steady load.
- Include a 10% path that invokes the reranker (simulated extra call).

Priyom, can you confirm infra availability 7/16 10:00 PT and whether we can run the synthetic load against a Dedicated trial instance or the hosted endpoint?

Thanks — M.
